newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia financial execs see 3.7 pct GDP in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Colombia financial execs see 3.7 pct GDP in 1997.

text.p: Colombia's finance chiefs forecast gross domestic product, fueled by mining and oil, would grow 3.7 percent in 1997, in their weekly report Monday.

The influential National Association of Financial Institutions (ANIF) predicted the Venezuelan economy would also pick up in 1997, thereby helping boost bilateral trade with Colombia, while a fall in interest rates, currently averaging about 28 percent, would stimulate direct investment.
The government has forecast GDP growth of between 4 percent and 4.5 percent this year, up from the 3 percent rise in GDP, one of the lowest this decade, recorded in 1996.
"There are some relatively solid factors that allow us to forecast the recovery of the Colombian economy this year," ANIF said in its report.

The organization, made up of banks and financial groups, predicted retail sales and industrial output would grow 2 percent in 1997. Year-end figures for 1996 have not yet been released by the government's National Statistics Department.
It also predicted the labor-intensive construction industry would show signs of growth in the second half of this year.

The association, however, sounded a word of warning, saying that the build-up to the 1998 presidential elections could create political uncertainty as campaigning got under way towards the end of the year.
It added that the U.S. decision on whether to recertify Colombia as an ally in the drug war -- expected in March -- could also have an economic impact.
Conflict between leftist rebels and the army, which some military experts and politicians expect will intensify this year, could also scare off foreign investors, ANIF said.
